chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: Saving money and deciding to look up Gladys Mosier
summary: The club began to draw performers like Gladys Mosier's Ina Ray Hutton band, which led to her New York plan.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: A year. I stayed there a year. And in the meantime the clientele began to change because Obie went out and told all the local musicians
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

and performers to come up to the club and we began to have quite a few performers as clients. And I know that when the bands would come to Pittsburgh they'd wind up there. And I received an awful lot of encouragement from the bands like Artie Shaw, some of the bands that were playing at the hotel like Dick Stabile, Woody Herman. Whatever bands were playing at the time, they would wind up at the club and I received an awful lot of encouragement from them. And of course, this is where I met Gladys Moser. I know he had his band in town. And Gladys wound up at the club and I was talking with her.
Hutton led an all female orchestra.

Yeah. And so Gladys said, if you ever come to New York look me up. So that sort of put the idea in my head that I might have a chance, you know, to really do something. And I suppose by that time I was sounding a little bit like Ella, maybe Billie in doing things like that. I was certainly doing their songs. And Martha Raye was popular at the time. And I was doing all the currently popular tunes. So I started
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

saving my money and at the end of the year I said to Jenny, I said, look, I'm going to go to New York. And so naturally she wanted to come too. And in those days they had Sunday excursions to New York, overnight excursions. So I went to work like Saturday night and the excursion would leave Sunday morning early, and leave Monday morning going back to Pittsburgh. So I spoke to Obie and I said, look I'm going to New York. If I make it I won't be back. And if I don't make it I'll be back Monday, and don't say anything to anybody because I didn't want to have to come back and say I didn't make it. I don't know what ever gave me the idea that I was going to come to New York and in one day, you know, set the world on fire.

It did, and I came to New York and Gladys Mosier's band was playing at the Paramount Theatre. We located her and she said, well look, you can't go back right away. It takes time. So she said, why don't you stay until around Wednesday. Stay a couple of days and I'll see what I can do. So sure enough, Wednesday I met with Gladys and I was staying at 409
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

Comb Avenue with Jenny's brother, Mardo Brown, he was an entertainer at the Cotton Club. So she came up and we auditioned in every gin mill from 155th Street down to the Onyx Club. And she introduced me to Claude Thron-hill.
And that starts a new chapter.
